checks: Affine sampled value vectors form a closed finite-dimensional linear subspace. The coordinate floors are positive. The constant maximum root is feasible, and any bounded objective sublevel supplies upper coordinate bounds, so compactness gives attainment.
For q>1 the sum of powers is strictly convex on the positive orthant. Two distinct attaining vectors would have a feasible midpoint of strictly smaller objective. No uniqueness is asserted for q=1.

Each feasible coordinate contributes at least V_z. Equality in the sum holds exactly when all coordinates equal their roots, including q=1, so A_q=1 exactly for affine sampled roots. The constant maximum root gives the stated upper bound.

For an attaining L, ell=τ^(1/q)L is nonnegative on conv(P) because it is nonnegative on the generators. This includes τ=0. It is finite and convex, and its q-power at every sampled base dominates τV_z, so the same original cap family satisfies the predecessor's local hypothesis.

The predecessor gives at most kt caps and total allowance τΣL(z)^q=τA_qM. For nonnegative B, its budget gives (1−τA_q)M/(kt). If t=2 and q=d, the condition τA_d≤1−2γ_d yields the claimed bound. Equal-volume planar roots are constant and give A_2=1, so τ≤1/9.

The pinned source locator 2623b39acd3d4a1d:03, §4 (5)–(7) and the final paragraph of §7, supports the optimization and its intrinsic extension. The converse to A_q=1 is immediate from the independently checked coordinatewise equality argument.
